turns.doctor_question: Was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing the dispatch voices even though you were not feeling depressed?
turns.patient_response:
Well, yeah, there was a time... I guess it was a few months back. My mood had actually eased up a bit, you know? I wasn't feeling so down in the dumps, and I was eating a little more, talking a bit more with my wife. We even went out to dinner once, to this little Italian place over on Main Street. Luigi's, I think it's called. They have this garlic bread that is just out of this world. They bake it with real butter, not that cheap margarine stuff, and they load it up with parmesan cheese. You can smell it before they even bring it to the table. The waiter we had, he was a young kid, maybe early twenties, going to the community college. He said he was studying criminal justice, wanted to be a state trooper. I told him he'd better get used to drinking bad coffee on the night shift. My buddy Dave was a cop for thirty years, and he always complained about the coffee at the station. He said it tasted like battery acid. Dave actually retired down to Arizona a few years ago. He bought this RV, one of those huge Class A motorhomes, and he just drives around the desert. He sends me pictures sometimes. The sunsets out there are incredible, all purple and orange. But I don't think I could handle the heat. I mean, dry heat or not, 110 degrees is just too hot. You can't even go outside without feeling like you're in an oven. I prefer having four seasons, even if the winters get a little rough. Last winter we had that ice storm that knocked out the power for three days. We had to huddle around the fireplace...

But, uh, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the voices. Yeah, so even during that stretch when my mood was better and I was eating and talking more, for several weeks I was still hearing the dispatch calling my number. Clear as a bell. And I still knew the routing system was tracking me, even when I wasn't feeling depressed.
